## Verdict: **REJECT** for recording

Not a close call, but not a reflexive one either — the writing is better than most scripts I'd gate. It fails on a small number of defects that a listener, with no ability to re-read, will actually trip over.

---

### What's working

- **Transitions are genuinely good and load-bearing.** "Which brings us to the awkward part." / "Then you run it and watch." / "The reason all of this is arriving at once is that two very different timescales met." These are spoken-register handoffs, not written ones. Nothing is stitched with "furthermore."
- **Restraint.** No hype adjectives, no "revolutionary," no manufactured stakes. "Nobody drew that layout on a whiteboard. It is there because it kept flies alive." earns its effect by being the only flourish in the paragraph.
- **Ring composition.** The close returns to "a network architecture that came from an animal," which is the opening question. The shape of the story is sound.
- **Prerequisite ordering is mostly correct.** Neuron → synapse → connectome → how the map is made → what you download → equations → adapter. A listener is never asked to hold an undefined bio term.

---

### Blocking defects

**1. Name collision in audio — second paragraph.**
> "At the sports betting company bet three sixty-five... We call the project bet three sixty fly"

Two sentences apart, differing by one syllable. On the page these are distinct; read aloud they will be heard as the same string, and the listener loses the company/project distinction for the rest of the piece. This is the most concrete audio defect in the script.

**2. Dangling clause that dead-ends.**
> "Both teams are encoded by the same rules and presented separately, so one team tasting good never requires the other to taste bad, using only information available before the game."

The trailing modifier attaches to the tasting clause, where it means nothing. It's a data-leakage claim stapled onto a symmetry claim. A reader can reconstruct the intent; a listener cannot, and the sentence ends with them holding a fragment.

**3. The script opens a question about its own thesis and drops it.**
Three components are disclosed as hand-placed:
> "a set of neurons we chose in advance"

> "a small external model, trained on past seasons, turns the two patterns into a prediction"

...plus the engineered taste-pathway mapping. These sit against:
> "Nobody drew that layout on a whiteboard."

The narration is admirably honest about each piece, but never reconciles them. A listener who is paying attention arrives at "so which part is the fly?" and the script moves on to plasticity. Whatever the answer is, the script has to acknowledge the question it raised.

**4. Result-paragraph ordering lands as damage control.**
> "it called about fifty-six percent correctly, level with a conventional model given the same pregame information. This is a historical prediction experiment. Its purpose is to help us investigate how biological wiring processes information from a different world."

The purpose reframe arrives *after* the number. Sequenced this way, it reads as a retreat rather than as the premise the experiment was built on. This is an ordering fault, not a problem with the number.

**5. Aside with no antecedent.**
> "Some browser demos use JavaScript to animate scripted movement, even when a dopamine meter appears beside the fly."

The listener has never seen these demos and has no idea what the dopamine meter refers to. It reads as an unnamed swipe at someone, and it interrupts the DOOMFLY point rather than supporting it.

---

### Audience: mostly consistent, one clear inversion

The inferred audience is **working engineers / ML-literate listeners who don't know neuroscience** — and the script mostly serves them well. "If you work with embeddings, the shape will be familiar" is a graceful conditional gloss.

But the calibration inverts here:
> "mouse visual cortex, the brain tissue that processes vision"

is glossed, while in the same piece
> "a head reads the representation"

is not. One line explains what visual cortex is; another assumes "head" as a term of art. Pick a direction.

---

### Non-blocking — fix if convenient, don't hold the session

- The FlyVis/FlyBody paragraph is the pacing sag: two dense capability descriptions ending in an abstract payoff ("what a future connectome-derived controller with eyes and legs would have to handle").
- "HHMI Janelia, the University of Cambridge, and the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology" — necessary attribution, but the densest sentence in the first third when spoken.
- Two exact dates ("the eighth of June," "the third of September") are low-value detail in audio.
- The final sentence stacks "a growing library" and "increasingly accompanied" — two growth words in one clause, and the clause is long for a closer.
- The plasticity section ends by restating its own result ("The next presentation of a cue now encounters a circuit changed by its previous experience"), and its relevance to the baseball pipeline is left implicit — "a separate version of our simulator" signals it wasn't used there, but doesn't say so.

Fix items 1–5 and this is a recordable script.
